key_terms.meaning: Safe strain a sheet can take before local necking or tearing.
σ = K ε^n; σ is true stress, ε is true strain, K is strength coefficient; high n delays necking.
r = width strain ÷ thickness strain; r̄ = (r0 + 2r45 + r90)/4; high r̄ resists thinning.
Plot of major versus minor surface strain at necking; strains below the curve are safe.
Shearing a hole in a sheet; the removed slug is scrap.
Shearing a closed contour from sheet; the removed slug is the product.
Gap per side between punch and die; it controls cut-edge quality and burr.
BA = θ(R + K t); θ in radians, R inside radius, t thickness, K neutral-axis factor.
Elastic recovery after bending; the bend angle opens and radius increases.
Layer in a bend with no length change; it is used in bend allowance.
Pulling a flat blank into a die with a punch to form a cup; flange compresses and wall thins.
Blank diameter ÷ cup diameter in deep drawing; high ratio means a severe draw.
Clamping force on the flange; it suppresses wrinkles without stopping the draw.
Thinning the cup wall by forcing the cup through a clearance smaller than wall thickness.
Clamped sheet is stretched over a form block by tensile force.
Pressing sheet between matched dies to raise shallow surface detail without large thickness change.
Closed-die pressing that copies fine detail and changes thickness locally.
Cyclic process: melt polymer is injected into a closed mould, cooled and ejected.
Continuous process: melt polymer is forced through a die to make constant cross-section.
Mass of polymer extruded through a standard die in 10 min; higher MFI means easier flow.

takeaways: Formability is limited by necking or tearing, and n, r̄ and the FLD help judge safe strain.
Punching and blanking use the same shear tool, but the product is a hole in punching and the slug in blanking.
A bent part needs bend allowance in the blank length, and springback is corrected by overbending.
Deep drawing needs controlled draw ratio and blank holder force; ironing thins the cup wall.
Stretch forming uses tension over a form block, while embossing and coining use closed dies; coining changes thickness.
Thermoplastics are shaped by injection moulding in cycles and by extrusion continuously.
Defects link to process variables: wrinkles and tears in drawing, burr in shearing, short shots in moulding.
Process choice depends on batch size, shape, material and required surface detail.
bank_note: Long answers usually stress labelled tooling sketches, process steps, defect causes and remedies, and numerical checks such as bend allowance, punch force and draw ratio; some syllabi also add ironing and hydroforming under deep drawing.

bank.q: Define sheet-metal formability. Explain how strain hardening exponent n, normal anisotropy r̄ and a forming limit diagram are used to judge whether a sheet can be formed safely.
outline: role of n in delaying necking
role of r̄ in resisting thinning
axes and safe region of FLD

bank.q: Compare punching and blanking with a neat sketch. Explain the function of punch, die, clearance and stripper, and state what happens to the slug in each operation.
Explain bending of sheet metal. State the bend allowance formula and describe springback and overbending.
Describe deep drawing of a cylindrical cup. Define draw ratio, blank holder force and ironing, and explain the role of each.
outline: draw ratio = blank diameter ÷ cup diameter

bank.q: Distinguish stretch forming, embossing and coining. Give one typical product for each and state whether sheet thickness changes.
outline: stretch forming uses tension over form block
embossing uses matched dies for shallow detail
coining uses closed dies and changes thickness

bank.q: Describe injection moulding and extrusion of thermoplastics. Compare cyclic and continuous operation and name the main machine parts.
A 2.0 mm thick sheet is bent to 90° with inside bend radius 4.0 mm. Take K = 0.33. Calculate bend allowance. State the blank length contribution if the two straight legs are 50 mm and 30 mm.
A 20 mm diameter hole is punched in 3 mm thick mild steel with shear strength 300 MPa. Calculate punching force. Explain how clearance affects burr and tool life.
outline: small clearance raises force and tool wear
large clearance gives burr and poor edge

bank.q: A 100 mm diameter blank is deep drawn into a 50 mm diameter cup. Calculate draw ratio. Explain why a blank holder is needed and what happens if its force is too high or too low.
For a plastic bucket and a plastic pipe, choose between injection moulding and extrusion. Describe the mould or die and the cycle or line, and justify each choice.
A deep-drawn cup tears near the punch corner while another batch wrinkles at the flange. Analyze the likely causes in terms of draw ratio, blank holder force, clearance, lubrication, n and r̄.
outline: wrinkling from low blank holder force
high n and high r̄ help

bank.q: A bent bracket shows springback and a sheared blank shows a rough burr. Analyze the process variables that cause both defects and propose practical remedies.

Evaluate stretch forming, deep drawing and coining for an automobile body panel that needs a large smooth surface plus a fine badge detail. Discuss formability limits, tooling cost, thickness change and production rate.
outline: stretch forming for large smooth panels
coining for fine detail and thickness change

glossary.def: The safe amount of strain a sheet can take before local necking or tearing.
Increase in strength as a metal is plastically strained.
Directional variation in sheet properties, especially strain ratio r.
A map of major and minor surface strains that separates safe forming from necking.
The male tool that pushes into the sheet or die.
The female tool that shapes, cuts or supports the sheet.
The flat sheet piece from which a part is cut or formed.
The piece removed by punching or the part produced by blanking.
The gap per side between punch and die in a shearing tool.
A rough edge left on a sheared or cut part.
The inside radius of a bend in sheet metal.
The length of the neutral axis in a bend, added to straight lengths to get blank size.
Elastic recovery that makes a bent part open slightly after load removal.
Forming a cup from a flat blank by pulling it into a die with a punch.
Blank diameter divided by cup diameter in deep drawing.
The ring that presses the flange to prevent wrinkles during deep drawing.
Reducing cup wall thickness by pushing it through a tight clearance.
Compressive buckling of sheet, usually in the flange during drawing.
Local fracture caused by excessive tensile strain during forming.
Shaping a clamped sheet by stretching it over a form block.
Raising shallow lettering or pattern on sheet by pressing between matched dies.
Closed-die pressing that reproduces fine detail and changes thickness locally.
A cyclic plastics process that fills a closed mould with melt and ejects the cooled part.
A continuous plastics process that forces melt through a die to make constant cross-section.
A polymer that softens on heating and can be remelted and reshaped.
A moulding defect in which melt does not fill the whole cavity.
